newsitem.title: USA: High-grade US corporate bonds outshine junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: High-grade US corporate bonds outshine junk bonds.

text.p: High-grade corporate bond market players saw signs of market strength on Tuesday, while their counterparts in the high-yield market had cause for concern, traders said.
Investment-grade corporate issuers sold over $1 billion in new bonds and a bid list of $1.5 billion of high-grade bonds was easily absorbed in the secondary market, traders said.
"The bid list traded very aggressively. This shows there is pretty good underlying strength in the market and bodes well for the future," said one high-grade trader.
Spreads remained unchanged on the day, they said.
But weakness in the Treasury and stock markets triggered a half-point drop in high-yield bond prices across the board late in the day, traders said.
"This was a tough day to be a junk bond trader. Greenspan has made people very spread-sensitive and the Treasury sell-off hurt our market."
Several new issues in the junk bond market also traded down or flat soon after they were priced, traders said.
Revlon Worldwide zero coupon bonds were quoted at 64 5/8 after pricing at 65.59 on Friday. McCaw International's zeros, priced yesterday, were trading at issue price, traders said.
Traders reported no bids on the only issue that priced in the junk bond market today -- a $300 million exchangeable preferred stock deal from Intermedia Communications Inc.
The securities, which initially do not pay cash but pay in similar securities, priced with a 13.5 percent coupon via Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Back in the high-grade market, Tennesee Gas Pipeline sold $900 million in bonds via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
The three-part deal included a 20-year, 40-year and a 30-year tranche. The 30-year tranche was puttable in 10 years.
Fluor Corp also sold $300 million in 6.95 percent 10-year notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.

In secondary market trading, junk bonds of Home Holdings Inc dropped 12 points on news that the New Hampshire Insurance Department had placed its principal subsidiary, Home Insurance Co, under formal supervision, traders said.

Elsewhere, the Claridge Hotel and Casino Corp announced that it had reached an agreement with bondholders to avoid bankruptcy. The company also said that it would make the 11 3/4 coupon payment on the $85 million in bonds.
Traders said the New York Stock Exchange halted trading on the bonds. One trader, who said the bonds were last trading at 85.6, said their price should rise substantially when trading resumes.
In the Treasury market, the price of the 30-year long-bond dropped 14/32 to 96-29/32. The yield rose to 6.87 percent.
